record.paper_title: Invitation to H-systems in higher dimensions: known results, new facts, and related open problems
record.original_question: Let B be a ball, let u be in W^{1,n}(B,R^m), and suppose u solves -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = Omega · |grad u|^{n-2} grad u, where Omega takes values in so(m) tensor R^n and belongs to the Lorentz space L^{(n,p)}. For which p in the interval [1,n] does this assumption imply that u is necessarily continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3. Let u ∈ W 1,n (B, Rm ) be a solution to (2.6) for where Ω is an L(n,p) -matrix with values in so(m) ⊗ Rn . For which p ∈ [1, n] is u necessarily continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$, $m \geq 1$, and let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be the open unit ball. Consider a map $u \in W^{1,n}(B,\mathbb{R}^m)$ that solves, in the distributional sense, the critical $n$-Laplace system
$$ -\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{n-2}\,\nabla u\bigr) \;=\; \Omega \cdot |\nabla u|^{n-2}\,\nabla u \qquad \text{in } B,$$
where the potential $\Omega = (\Omega^{i}_{j,\alpha})_{1\le i,j\le m,\,1\le\alpha\le n}$ takes values in $\mathfrak{so}(m) \otimes \mathbb{R}^n$ (i.e.\ $\Omega^{i}_{j,\alpha} = -\Omega^{j}_{i,\alpha}$ for all $i,j,\alpha$), and the right-hand side is interpreted as $(\Omega\cdot |\nabla u|^{n-2}\nabla u)^i = \sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{\alpha=1}^{n}\Omega^{i}_{j,\alpha}\,|\nabla u|^{n-2}\,\partial_\alpha u^j$.

Assume that the components of $\Omega$ belong to the Lorentz space $L^{(n,p)}(B)$ for some $p \in [1,n]$. Recall that $L^{(n,p)}(B)$ consists of measurable functions $f$ on $B$ for which the quasinorm
$$\|f\|_{L^{(n,p)}} = \left(\int_0^\infty \bigl(t^{1/n} f^{*}(t)\bigr)^{p}\,\frac{dt}{t}\right)^{1/p}$$
is finite (with the usual modification for $p=\infty$), where $f^{*}$ denotes the decreasing rearrangement of $|f|$.

Determine the precise set of exponents $p \in [1,n]$ such that, for every choice of $u$ and $\Omega$ as above, the solution $u$ is necessarily continuous on $B$.
artifact.status_search_result: Continuity of solutions has been established under the stronger Lorentz-space assumption $\Omega \in L^{(n,2)}$ (in particular giving continuity of critical $n$-harmonic maps whose gradient lies in $L^{(n,2)}$), as shown by Martino and Schikorra (Math. Ann., 2023; arXiv:2305.05961). However, the full range $p \in (2,n]$ does not appear to be settled in the literature, so the complete characterization of admissible $p$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing properties of n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials in Lorentz spaces
status_evidence.snippet: We show continuity of solutions ... when Ω is an L^n-antisymmetric potential and additionally satisfies a Lorentz-space assumption. n-harmonic maps into manifolds are continuous if their gradient belongs to the Lorentz space L^(n,2), the weakest assumption to date.
status_evidence.claim: Continuity is established under an L^(n,2) Lorentz-space hypothesis, leaving the regime up to p=n not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing properties of n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials in Lorentz spaces (Math. Ann.)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version in Mathematische Annalen establishing continuity via L^(n,2)-type assumptions and Coulomb gauge methods.
status_evidence.claim: Best published continuity result corresponds to p=2; broader p remains unresolved.
